The equation is \(x^{10} + (13x-1)^{10} = 0\). Rearranging gives \((13x-1)^{10} = -x^{10}\). Taking the 10th root yields \(13x-1 = \omega x\), where \(\omega\) is a 10th root of \(-1\) (i.e., \(\omega^{10} = -1\)). Thus the roots are \(x = \frac{1}{13-\omega}\) for each of the 10 distinct roots \(\omega_k\) of \(-1\).

The magnitude squared of a root is
\[
|x|^2 = x\overline{x} = \frac{1}{(13-\omega)(13-\overline{\omega})} = \frac{1}{169 - 13(\omega+\overline{\omega}) + |\omega|^2}.
\]
Since \(|\omega|=1\), this simplifies to
\[
|x|^2 = \frac{1}{170 - 26\,\text{Re}(\omega)}.
\]
Hence \(\frac{1}{|x|^2} = 170 - 26\,\text{Re}(\omega)\).

The sum of \(\frac{1}{|x|^2}\) over all 10 roots is
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{9} \bigl(170 - 26\,\text{Re}(\omega_k)\bigr) = 10 \cdot 170 - 26\,\text{Re}\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{9} \omega_k\right).
\]
The sum of all 10th roots of \(-1\) is zero (they are the roots of \(z^{10}+1=0\), whose \(z^9\) coefficient is 0). Therefore the sum over all 10 roots is \(1700\).

The 10 roots come in 5 conjugate pairs \(\{r_i, \overline{r_i}\}\). For each pair, \(|r_i|^2 = |\overline{r_i}|^2 = r_i\overline{r_i}\). The desired sum is
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{5} \frac{1}{r_i\overline{r_i}} = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{\text{all 10 roots}} \frac{1}{|x|^2} = \frac{1700}{2} = 850.
\]

Answer: 850
